question: In the lecture, what is the temperature setting?

options.text: A little noise added before the next token is chosen from the probabilities
options.feedback: Temperature is the small nudge applied at the very end, when one token is picked from the distribution. It is what lets the model take a slightly different path through the same probabilities each time.

options.text: A filter that removes implausible tokens before the choice is made
options.feedback: Implausible tokens already have probabilities near zero, so nothing needs to filter them out. Temperature does the opposite of narrowing: it adds noise so that a less-than-top token sometimes gets chosen.

options.text: A dial that changes how much of the context attention reads
options.feedback: Attention always looks back over the whole context, and no setting shortens that. Temperature acts after every stack has finished, at the moment of choosing a token, not while meaning is being computed.

options.text: A setting for how many decoder stacks the embedding passes through
options.feedback: The number of decoder stacks is fixed by the model's architecture, and it is part of what makes a model large or small. Temperature touches none of that; it only affects the final choice of a token.
